# Ask Krishna

> A quiet way to reflect with the Bhagavad Gita, and to read all 18 chapters online.

Live site: https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/

Ask Krishna has two parts:

- Reflect (home page): begin with the Hare Krishna mahamantra and a short purification verse, hold your question silently (it is never typed, sent or stored), then open the Bhagavad Gita to a passage of three verses. Five passages is the suggested limit; if none answers, the app suggests it may be time to wait.
- Read Gita: all 18 chapters, one verse at a time, with the Sanskrit text and an English or Hindi meaning, bookmarks, and your reading position remembered on your device.

The site is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. There are no accounts.

## Pages

- Home / reflection: https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/
- Read the Bhagavad Gita: https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/pages/read.html (701 verses in this edition, one verse at a time; a verse opens at `read.html#2.47`)

## Data (MIT-licensed; see NOTICE.md)

- Verse structure and Sanskrit: `/data/verses.json` — array of 701 objects `{ "id": "chapter.verse", "chapter": N, "verse": N, "sanskrit": "..." }`
- English translations: `/data/translations/en.json` — map `{ "1.1": "...", ... }`
- Hindi translations: `/data/translations/hi.json` — same shape
- UI strings per language: `/assets/locales/<code>.json` (codes: en, hi, sa)

## License and attribution

- App code: MIT — see `/LICENSE`
- Dataset source and translation attributions: see `/NOTICE.md`

## Suggested use for agents

Fetch `/data/verses.json` for Sanskrit text and structure. Fetch `/data/translations/en.json` or `/data/translations/hi.json` for readable translations. Verse IDs use the format `chapter.verse` (e.g. `2.47`). For a whole chapter as readable HTML, use the chapter pages listed above.
